test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements regarding small scale industries in India is correct?

options.text: They are classified based on number of workers employed.
They are identified by annual turnover only.
They are classified based on capital investment in assets.
They are defined solely by export volume.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are classified based on capital investment in assets.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Small-scale industries (SSIs) in India are primarily classified based on their investment in plant and machinery or equipment.
 
• According to the **Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006**, the classification of SSIs is defined by the investment in fixed assets, such as plant and machinery for manufacturing enterprises and equipment for service enterprises.
 
• As per the revised criteria effective from July 2020, small enterprises are defined as those with an investment of up to **Rs. 10 crores** and annual turnover of up to **Rs. 50 crores**.
 
• This classification helps the government in providing targeted subsidies, tax benefits, and incentives to small-scale enterprises.
 
• Small-scale industries play a vital role in employment generation, regional development, and fostering entrepreneurship in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Classified based on the number of workers employed**

 
 
• This classification is not used for defining small-scale industries in India.
 
• The number of workers employed is typically used for categorizing industries as labor-intensive or capital-intensive, but it is not a formal criterion for SSI classification.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Identified by annual turnover only**
 
 
• While annual turnover is a key parameter under the revised MSME criteria (2020), it is not the sole factor for defining SSIs.
 
• Investment in assets remains the primary determinant for classification.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Defined solely by export volume**
 
 
• Export volume is not a criterion for identifying or classifying SSIs in India.
 
• Export-oriented units (EOUs) are a separate category and are not synonymous with SSIs.
